runs.t: A Repository presents a collection-like interface for domain objects and hides persistence operations. It aims to separate business policy from query mechanics, not to pretend all databases are interchangeable.

Design operations around use cases or aggregates, such as findAvailableRooms and saveReservation. Keep transactional semantics explicit and avoid leaking ORM query builders into the domain; complex analytics may belong to dedicated query services.
A booking repository ensures reservation records are retrieved and saved consistently, while a report query reads optimized projections without loading rich aggregates.

A generic CRUD repository can hide useful database features and create inefficient access. ORM libraries often already expose repository behavior; wrap them only when it protects meaningful policy boundaries.
